architecture.approach: The stack already works, so this plan adds one service, one script, one configuration key and one document rather than restructuring anything. MongoDB is declared now because BP-031 needs it and a declared service is cheaper than a discovered gap; no application code reads it in this version. The bootstrap is a Node script because Windows is a first-class developer environment here and Node 20 is already a prerequisite, so a second toolchain is not introduced. .env.example stays the single source of values: the bootstrap copies examples and never synthesises a credential.

components.name: docker-compose.yml
components.description: Add a mongo service (mongo:7-alpine, port 27017, healthcheck, named volume riaya_mongodata) beside the existing postgres and redis services, leaving both untouched.

components.name: scripts/setup-env.mjs
components.description: Idempotent bootstrap: for server, web and backoffice, copy .env.example to .env only when .env is absent; report created, skipped or missing example per package; exit 0.

components.name: package.json
components.description: Add the root script "setup": "node scripts/setup-env.mjs" without renaming or reordering existing scripts.

components.name: server/.env.example
components.description: Document the MongoDB connection key beside REDIS_URL with a local default and no real credential.

components.name: README.md
components.description: Rewrite the quick start around pnpm setup and add troubleshooting for the Docker prerequisite and the default ports.

components.name: .gitignore
components.description: Already ignores .env while keeping .env.example tracked; verified, not changed.

components.name: web/.env.example
components.description: Exists and is consumed by the bootstrap as-is.

components.name: backoffice/.env.example
components.description: Exists and is consumed by the bootstrap as-is.

dataModel.flowDescription: No schema change: prisma/schema.prisma is untouched and the MongoDB service stores nothing in this version. Flow: pnpm install, pnpm setup creates the three .env files, docker compose up -d brings postgres, redis and mongo to healthy, pnpm dev serves web on 3000, the API on 4000 and the backoffice on 5173.

securityConsiderations.description: Only .env.example files are committed (CON-519, CON-504, CON-505). The bootstrap writes .env files that .gitignore already excludes, copies example values verbatim and never generates or stores a credential; no .env is ever opened by the tooling (CON-502, CON-503).

performanceConsiderations.strategy: The five-minute target is measured once on the documented prerequisites with a warm image cache and recorded as evidence; if the run disagrees, the README claim is corrected rather than the measurement.
Every compose service declares a healthcheck, so readiness is a real signal rather than container start, and the 60-second expectation is observable with docker compose ps.

dependencies.name: MongoDB 7
dependencies.notes: Compose service only; no client library is added in this version.

dependencies.name: Docker Compose
dependencies.notes: Already required by the postgres and redis services.

dependencies.name: Node.js node:fs
dependencies.notes: Built in; the bootstrap adds no package.

risks.description: Developers with an existing server/.env never receive the new MongoDB key.
risks.mitigation: The bootstrap reports skipped files and the README names the key to add by hand (EC-003).

risks.description: A third container makes local startup feel slower.
risks.mitigation: Healthchecks on every service and the documented 60-second expectation (NFR-003).

risks.description: The five-minute claim drifts into marketing.
risks.mitigation: NFR-001 records one timed run and the README is corrected if it disagrees.
